name: Counter-TS-TW
title: Animated Number Counter
description: A large metric rolls its digits upward like slot reels, one place at a time, with the top and bottom of the row fading out. A smaller count beside plus and minus buttons steps by one when pressed.
use: A dashboard statistic should feel live and draw the eye without the weight of a chart.
avoid: Every digit position is listed by hand, so decimals, currency signs and odd formats take extra setup.
a11y: The changing digits are plain text with no aria-live region, so assistive tech never hears the new value. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A small grey caption sits above a wide row of very large white numerals. Below it, a round outlined minus and plus button bracket a smaller two-digit number, and the big digits fade slightly at their top and bottom edges.
behaves: Each digit spins vertically from the old value to the new one and settles. Pressing plus or minus steps the lower number by one, while the upper figure also climbs on its own in the demo.
customise: Value and place values, size, padding, gap, weight, colours, radius and the top and bottom fade are props; the spin itself is fixed.
weight: light: Roughly fifty small spans for five digits, each on a spring, idle between value changes.
demo: Caption 'Visitors today', a five-digit visitor figure near 48,000, and a two-digit count beside plus and minus buttons.
issues: The digit fade defaults to black, so it paints dark bars unless the page background colour is passed.
polishWhy: Crisp big numerals and a convincing roll, though the two bare counters make a thin showcase.
